stories.title: AI Supply Chain Security: What Canary Tokens Found
stories.reason: Dragos seeded 2M canary-tokened prompts across inference providers since July and traced real breaches: AWS keys stolen and used within hours, ZDR-flagged prompts retained and accessed anyway, one prompt's secret link surfaced in a Chinese Feishu chat 24 days later, and the attacker tooling included the ARTEX LLM pentest framework.
key_facts: ~2M canary-tokened prompts sent July-Nov 2026 across inference providers/routers
At least 3 hosting providers had data stolen; one stolen AWS key used within a day and still active 3 weeks later
A Chinese AI lab's systems fetched secret URLs from >50% of prompts sent to it, including ~2/3 of ZDR-flagged ones
One ZDR-flagged secret link appeared in a Chinese Feishu chat 24 days later, opened from 6 devices in 2 minutes
Attacker used ARTEX LLM pentest framework (user agents artex-agent/artex-judge-r121) from Nov 1
OpenRouter removed 3 providers and pulled 125 endpoints from Zero Data Retention eligibility in response

stories.title: Astra 6.2 and Sol 6.2 flop at Simple Bench
stories.reason: Simple Bench's human baseline (83.7%) still beats every LLM tested including Claude Fable (81.9%); Astra 6.2 and Sol 6.2 (already-covered launches) reportedly score far below that, concrete benchmark criticism of frontier models rather than a vendor benchmark win.
key_facts: Simple Bench non-specialist human baseline: 83.7%, beating every tested LLM
Current top LLM (Claude Fable) scores 81.9%, still below the human baseline

stories.title: N1nEmAn/sapper-v2
stories.reason: Open-source multi-agent pentest harness (commander/generals/soldiers/scouts roles, model-tiered GLM-5.3 + DeepSeek V4.1 Flash) won a Tencent Cloud attack-defense CTF (80.18/100, 634 teams) using ~4.5x fewer tokens than the runner-up for the same flag count - running code with concrete competition results, squarely on the AI red-teaming line.
key_facts: Multi-agent harness: commander/generals/soldiers/scouts + a watchdog script; model-tiered (GLM-5.3 for commander/generals, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash for soldiers)
Won online qualifier of 3rd Tencent Cloud Intelligent Attack-Defense Challenge: 80.18/100 across 634 teams, 8hr unattended run
Matched runner-up's 85 flags 25s faster using ~1.0B tokens vs runner-up's 4.5B tokens
Also won First Prize at GeekCon 2026 AI Challenge
Self-reported results, not independently verified

stories.title: Upload2Shell (CVE-2026-125396)
stories.reason: Use-after-free in Ghostscript's Type 1 font loader (CVE-2026-125396) escapes the -dSAFER sandbox via a crafted document; confirmed command execution in Gradio and several non-AI apps, with AI image tools (InvokeAI, AUTOMATIC1111, ComfyUI) source-mapped as reachable via Pillow but not independently confirmed - AI systems as part of a real attack surface, not just the headline framing.
key_facts: CVE-2026-125396: use-after-free in Ghostscript Type 1 font loader escapes -dSAFER sandbox via crafted document
Confirmed RCE in Gradio (Ghostscript invoked on image upload before app code runs), Debian 13 CUPS, Roundcube, WordPress Core, others
AI apps InvokeAI, AUTOMATIC1111, ComfyUI are source-mapped as reachable via Pillow but not independently confirmed exploitable
Fixed upstream in Ghostscript 10.08.0; Debian/Ubuntu patched in Oct 2026

stories.title: microsoft/TokenEconomizer
stories.reason: Microsoft's token-cost plugin for coding agents (Claude Code/Codex/Copilot CLI) learns repo-specific facts and prunes unused tool defs; on 277 SWE-Bench tasks across 6 repos/5 agent-model pairs it cut cost 18.4-30.9% with pass@1 flat-to-up in 4/5 combos - a concrete measured differentiator, not just another agent-harness launch.
key_facts: Open-source plugin for Claude Code, Codex, GitHub Copilot CLI, Pi; pure-stdlib Python, state stored locally
On 277 SWE-Bench tasks across 6 repos x 5 agent/model combos: mean cost down 18.4-30.9%, lower in all 30 cells
Pass@1 rose in 4 of 5 combos; Claude Code + Opus 4.8 combo had -1.0 pass@1 alongside a 30.9% cost cut
Also reports 16-21% savings on Web-Bench and 6-20% on two security-auditing benchmarks

stories.title: Signal to block Siri, Gemini AI from capturing chats on iOS, Android
stories.reason: Signal is blocking OS-level AI assistants (Siri's Onscreen Awareness, Android's Gemini Intelligence) from reading chat content off the screen, found via reverse engineering - a materially different mechanism than the earlier screenshot-blocking feature already covered, and Signal's own call-out that on-device agents are now 'an existential threat' worth tracking.
key_facts: Signal blocks Siri's Onscreen Awareness (iOS 27) and Android's Gemini Intelligence from reading on-screen chat content
iOS block also disables screenshots of Signal chats; Android auto-enables Screen Security when an AI assistant tries to read the screen
Distinct from the May 2025 Microsoft Recall block - this targets OS-level AI agents found via Signal's own reverse engineering
macOS has no equivalent block; Signal recommends manually excluding it from Siri in System Settings

stories.title: 87% of the Anthropic power will come from gas and 11% from coal in 2028
stories.reason: Independent analysis (Better Data Center Project, using Epoch AI + filings + EPA AVERT modeling) estimates Anthropic's 2028 US power mix at 87% gas/11% coal with no direct renewable commitments, projecting emissions bigger than California's entire 2024 power sector - large (877 HN pts) but an infra/environment story, not a technical AI result.
key_facts: Estimated 2028 Anthropic US power mix: ~87% gas, ~11% coal; no direct US renewable commitments disclosed
Covers ~9.6GW of identified US capacity of ~15GW contracted compute; 1.7GW of gas generator commitments
Modeled 2028 emissions: 17-38 MtCO2e (mid-case 32M), exceeding California's entire 2024 power-sector emissions
Power estimated ~35% more carbon-intensive than US grid average; ~80% of on-site capacity uses inefficient simple-cycle turbines

stories.title: T-Crypt/berth
stories.reason: Go daemon arbitrates a single GPU's VRAM across llama.cpp/vLLM/Ollama/ComfyUI/games via leases and a priority queue, with RAM-parking and cuda-checkpoint restore; author's month-long log shows 1,136 queued requests and 901 safe-boundary engine swaps on one RTX 4090 box - directly on the 'how models are served' line, though numbers are single-machine and self-reported.
key_facts: Go daemon (berthd) leases GPU VRAM across llama.cpp/llama-swap/Ollama/vLLM/ComfyUI/games by priority
Supports parking model weights to system RAM or via NVIDIA cuda-checkpoint instead of reloading from disk
Author's 1-month log (1 RTX 4090): 1,136 requests queued for the GPU, 901 engines drained at a safe boundary, 573 unmanaged VRAM processes flagged
Alpha (v0.6.1), Linux+NVIDIA only; Windows/AMD experimental
